question: Should OpenClaw add a native child-session context-pressure notification and recovery contract, and if so should it notify only, wake the parent, route to alternates, or automatically recover saturated children?
rationale: The missing behavior is source-visible, but the requested fix adds new config/default and orchestration semantics that could affect existing subagent workflows and conflicts with VISION.md guardrails if implemented as a broad manager-of-managers layer.

options.title: Define Narrow Notification Contract
options.body: Add an owner-approved context-pressure signal that starts with parent/operator visibility and leaves recovery routing explicit or follow-up.

options.title: Fold Into Subagent Recovery Design
options.body: Track this under the broader subagent stall/circuit-breaker work so context pressure, blocked tool calls, and dropped completions share one recovery contract.

options.title: Defer For More Live Proof
options.body: Keep only the current status/reporting surfaces until a redacted live scenario proves the exact saturated-child failure and desired recovery behavior.

recommendation.title: Define Narrow Notification Contract
recommendation.body: Add an owner-approved context-pressure signal that starts with parent/operator visibility and leaves recovery routing explicit or follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans subagent parent/child semantics and session routing, where steipete has the strongest adjacent history among the inspected owners.
